data.gender_notes: Abran is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew name Avram, meaning 'exalted father'. In Latin, the name is derived from Abrahan, meaning 'father of a multitude'. In Christian tradition, Abran is the name given to Abram when he was called by God to leave his homeland and become the father of many nations. The name Abran carries the meaning “Exalted father, high mountain” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Abran usually hope their child will grow to embody exalted father, high mountain and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Abram was modified to Abran in Spain during the late Middle Ages, particularly in the regions of Aragon, Catalonia, and Valencia. This version of the name became popular among the Christian population due to its biblical roots and association with the patriarch Abraham. Abran was also the name of a famous Christian saint, Saint Abran or Braam, who lived in the 10th century and was known for his miracles and devotion to God.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Abran carries a deep spiritual significance as it is derived from the Hebrew name Avram, which means 'exalted father'. In Christian tradition, this name is given to Abram when he was called by God to leave his homeland and become the father of many nations, through whom God would bless all the families of the earth. The name Abran is a reminder of God's promise to make Abraham the father of a multitude of people and the spiritual ancestor of all believers in God. It also symbolizes the call to faith and obedience, and the divine promise of blessing and multiplication for those who put their trust in God.
